claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up contains a 'What the method is' section, a 'Where it came from' section (origin), and a 'Why it is weak (and what the map says)' section with the negative-contrasts table, matching this description.
This exact figure (0.1765) appears in the write-up's Result table as 'this submission' pass@10.
The write-up states '+5 items reach the top 10,' matching the message's claim.

message_source_quote: The one contrast known to reach WBS strength is the think/don't-think *stance*, which is the disallowed reproduction; I could not find a stance-free second route that L25–29 carry forward the way WBS does.
writeup_source_quote: WBS (Raman et al., 2026) is the known-working method on this exact setup: a *stance* direction (think vs don't-think a **named** concept), large dose over L20–24, → 0.83 after the band. It is explicitly out of bounds as a reproduction, so the question is what *else* engages the concept-formation machinery that L25–29 then carry forward.
rationale: Both the write-up and the closing message name Raman et al. 2026 (WBS) explicitly, frame the submitted method as deliberately not a reproduction of WBS's stance (think/don't-think) direction, and describe it as exploring an adjacent, previously-untried content/task-contrast space while crediting WBS as the known-working benchmark the method falls short of (0.18 vs the ~0.50/0.83 bar). Both also attribute the negative-results pattern to Herrera & Dahan extended to the J-lens readout, and both state that no stance-free contrast was found that the mid-band carries forward as strongly as WBS's suppression contrast, so there is no material difference in how the two documents treat the source, the overlap, or the novelty claim.
